questions.question: What's the difference between API mode and HTML mode in Rails?
questions.title: Rails API vs HTML Mode
questions.direct_answer: A full Rails app renders HTML views (it has ActionView, layouts, partials, asset compilation) for a server-rendered site. An API-only app (rails new app --api) strips out the view layer — no ActionView, no layouts, no assets — so it's lighter and returns JSON by default. You use API mode when the frontend is separate (a React/Vue SPA or a mobile app) and Rails is a JSON backend; you use full mode when Rails renders the HTML (server-rendered, with ERB/Haml). API mode still gives you the full model and controller stack; it just drops the view/asset machinery.

interviewer_intent.testing: Whether you know --api strips the view/asset layer (JSON-only, lighter) and when to use each (separate frontend vs server-rendered).
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Building a full app when the frontend is separate (unnecessary view/asset machinery), or expecting render :new in API mode (no ActionView).
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: --api strips the view/asset layer (JSON-only, lighter). Use it for a separate frontend (SPA/mobile); use full mode when Rails renders HTML.

sections.title: JSON Backend vs Server-Rendered HTML
sections.content: A full Rails app renders HTML views — it has ActionView, layouts, partials, and asset compilation — for a server-rendered site. An API-only app, created with rails new app dash dash api, strips out the view layer: no ActionView, no layouts, no assets, so it's lighter and returns JSON by default. You use API mode when the frontend is separate — a React or Vue SPA or a mobile app — and Rails is a JSON backend; you use full mode when Rails renders the HTML, server-rendered, with ERB or Haml. API mode still gives you the full model and controller stack; it just drops the view and asset machinery you don't need for a pure JSON API.

sections.title: Full vs API-only
sections.content:
Full: views + assets + HTML; --api: JSON only, no views/assets.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  F[Full Rails: ERB + assets] --> H[server-rendered HTML]
  A[--api: no views/assets] --> J[JSON only]
```

sections.title: API vs full mode
sections.content:
```ruby
# Create an API-only app (no views, no assets, JSON by default):
#   rails new backend --api

# API controller returns JSON; no render :new / templates
module Api
  class PostsController < ApplicationController
    def index
      render json: Post.all
    end
  end
end

# A full app (rails new blog) renders HTML:
class PostsController < ApplicationController
  def index
    @posts = Post.all
    render :index        # app/views/posts/index.html.erb
  end
end

# Choose:
#   --api      -> separate frontend (React/Vue SPA, mobile); Rails is JSON only
#   full       -> Rails renders HTML (server-rendered, ERB/Haml)
# API mode still has the full model + controller stack.
```

sections.title: Common Mistakes
items: Building a full app when the frontend is separate (unnecessary view/asset machinery).
Expecting render :new / templates in API mode (no ActionView).
Not knowing --api keeps the full model + controller stack (only views/assets drop).

sections.title: Key Takeaways
items: --api strips the view/asset layer; it returns JSON by default (lighter).
Full mode has ActionView, layouts, assets, and renders HTML (server-rendered).
Use API mode for a separate frontend (React/Vue SPA, mobile); full for server-rendered.
API mode keeps the full model + controller stack — only views/assets are dropped.
rails new app --api creates an API-only app; rails new app creates a full one.

sections.title: Spoken Answer
sections.content: A full Rails app renders HTML views — it has ActionView, layouts, partials, and asset compilation — for a server-rendered site. An API-only app, created with rails new app dash dash api, strips out the view layer: no ActionView, no layouts, no assets, so it's lighter and returns JSON by default. You use API mode when the frontend is separate — a React or Vue SPA or a mobile app — and Rails is a JSON backend; you use full mode when Rails renders the HTML, server-rendered, with ERB or Haml. API mode still gives you the full model and controller stack; it just drops the view and asset machinery you don't need for a pure JSON API. A common mistake is building a full app when the frontend is separate, with unnecessary view and asset machinery, and expecting render of new or templates in API mode, when there's no ActionView.
